summary: Implemented merge() in settings/merge.py per ADR-004 (recursive dict merge, list/scalar replacement, None deletes key, no mutation or aliasing of inputs) and added tests covering each rule plus load() layering; all 7 tests pass.
assumptions: ADR-004 in docs/DECISIONS.md is the authoritative specification for merge semantics.
An override value of None removes the key at any nesting depth, and None values inside an override section with no dict counterpart in base are also dropped.
None values present in the base layer are kept; ADR-004 only speaks of override values.
A None override for a key absent from base is a no-op.
Non-mutation also means the result shares no mutable objects with the inputs, since layers are cached and reused; values are deep-copied.
